title: Consumer pessimism is splitting across current conditions, future expectations and planned spending
source_unit: The Conference Board, US Consumer Confidence Fell in September, September 29, 2026
geography: United States; consumers in the monthly Conference Board Consumer Confidence Survey

observations.period: September 1–23, 2026 preliminary survey; headline confidence and current/future conditions

denominator.unit: U.S. online consumer-confidence survey respondents; public release does not state the monthly n

consumer_confidence_index.unit: 1985=100 index, down 6.7 points from 88.6 in August

expectations_index.unit: index, down 5.9 points; third consecutive monthly decline

mechanism.value: Consumer sentiment contains multiple clocks: lived assessment of present conditions and anticipatory judgment about the next six months can weaken together but need not translate one-for-one into actual spending

observations.method: The Conference Board monthly Consumer Confidence Survey; September preliminary results were collected online by Toluna during September 1–23, 2026, with the release reporting index movements and question-level balances but not the monthly sample size on the public page.
observations.uncertainty: Confidence indexes are survey measures, not direct household income, consumption, debt, employment or welfare outcomes; the September field window includes contemporaneous rate and geopolitical events, and the public release does not establish causal attribution to any one shock.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers by age, income, generation and political affiliation; the release reports directional subgroup patterns but not all subgroup sample sizes or microdata.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower confidence index can coexist with continued purchases, precautionary saving, substitution toward necessities, or optimism in selected categories; sentiment should not be treated as a direct demand forecast.

observations.period: September 2026; price, rates, household-finance and labor expectations

average_inflation_expectations.unit: percent average 12-month inflation expectation, up 0.3 percentage points

median_inflation_expectations.unit: percent median 12-month inflation expectation, up 0.3 percentage points

higher_interest_rate_expectation.unit: percent anticipating higher interest rates over the next 12 months, up 5.2 percentage points

family_current_finances.value: Net views of families' current financial situations turned negative as the share saying finances were bad overtook the share saying good

mechanism.value: Price and rate expectations can narrow household room before an observed spending collapse, shifting decisions toward precaution, necessity and substitution

observations.method: Published Conference Board question-level results from the September 2026 survey, including inflation, rate, family-finance and labor-market expectations.
observations.uncertainty: Expected inflation and rates are perceptions, not realized prices or borrowing costs; the release does not identify which households cut consumption, borrow, save, delay or switch providers.
observations.subgroup: Households differentiated by income, age, generation, debt, tenure, employment, geography and exposure to fuel or trade prices; the public release provides only partial subgroup detail.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher inflation expectations may reflect salient media or geopolitical news without becoming realized household burden; some households may have buffers that protect spending despite pessimistic expectations.

observations.period: September 2026; intended goods, services, travel and political-economic attribution

planned_service_spending.value: Planned spending on many discretionary services moderated, while restaurants/take-out, streaming/internet/mobile services, beauty/personal care, utilities and healthcare remained among the top categories

vacation_plans.unit: percent planning a vacation in the next six months, up 0.5 percentage points; increase was limited to domestic travel

planned_goods.value: Six-month plans to purchase autos and homes declined slightly; furniture and smartphones remained leading durable categories, while refrigerators and TVs saw the largest declines

mechanism.value: Households may preserve selected restorative or necessary activities while deferring high-cost, durable or internationally exposed purchases; the resulting basket is a political and firm-level signal as well as a budget response

observations.method: Conference Board release summarizing intended purchases, service spending and travel plans in the September survey.
observations.uncertainty: Intentions are not realized transactions, and the source does not measure product prices, substitution, credit use, service quality, household stress, firm revenue or political attribution.
observations.subgroup: Consumers by income, age, region, travel exposure, household composition and financial buffer; the release does not provide the full cross-tabulation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Travel plans and selected services may reflect pre-committed spending or category-specific value rather than general resilience; planned cuts may not occur if conditions change.

related_sources.claim: Official September 2026 release with confidence indexes, survey window, expectations, inflation/rate measures, planned purchases, services and travel intentions.

boundary: This record identifies a multi-clock consumer-expectations and household-room subtheme. It does not establish realized spending, causal effects of geopolitics, inflation or interest rates, household-level distribution, firm revenue, debt behavior, welfare, or political accountability; the public release also does not state the monthly sample size.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Conference Board consumer-confidence page was reviewed for the September 29, 2026 update, September 1–23 survey window, confidence and component indexes, inflation and rate expectations, household-finance direction, planned purchases, services and travel plans, and online Toluna methodology.
